lines: - Fix false positive `PhanPluginCaseMismatchNamespace` of `CaseMismatchPlugin` for a class name with a namespace that is not fully qualified, such as `DOM\Node` for the class `\Demo\DOM\Node` in the namespace `Demo`: the plugin compared it with the class `\DOM\Node` of the global namespace, which is `\Dom\Node` in PHP 8.4+. A casing mismatch in such a name is now reported against the class that the name refers to ([#5648](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5648))

- Fix false positive `PhanTypeMismatchReturnReal` and other issues caused by an outdated type of a static property after calling a method that assigns it with `self::`, `static::` or `parent::`, when Phan does not know the type that the method assigns: in `if (self::$prop === null) { self::setProp(new stdClass()); } return self::$prop;`, the type of `self::$prop` stayed `null` when `setProp()` was declared after the calling method (it is analyzed later), inherited from a parent class, or declared in a subclass of the class that declares the property. The property now has its previous type or its declared type after such a call, or an unknown type if it declares none ([#5651](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5651))

+- Fix false positive `PhanIncompatibleCompositionConstant` for a trait constant with the same name as a parent class constant when the parent constant is private, when the class using the trait declares the constant itself, or when `minimum_target_php_version` is 8.5 or newer (from PHP 8.5 on, a trait constant overrides a parent class constant). `PhanConstantTypeMismatchInheritance` now also checks public constants imported from traits, and, for `target_php_version` 8.3 or newer, reports an untyped constant that overrides a typed constant of a parent class or an interface, which PHP 8.3+ rejects. For a constant of an internal class, the type is the one of the PHP version running Phan: when that version is newer than a `target_php_version` of 8.3, this is not reported, because most internal constants got their type in PHP 8.4. Issues about a trait constant that overrides an inherited constant (`PhanConstantAccessSignatureMismatch`, `PhanAccessOverridesFinalConstant`, `PhanConstantTypeMismatchInheritance`) are reported at the class using the trait. `self` in the type of a constant of a trait is the class using the trait in the subclasses of that class too: overriding such a constant below an intermediate subclass with the type of that class was a false positive `PhanConstantTypeMismatchInheritance`. A constant that a class imports from a trait now takes precedence over a constant with the same name of an interface that the class implements, as in PHP: Phan used the constant of the interface for such a class, and did not check the constant of the trait against it (its type, `final` and its visibility) ([#5647](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5647))

- Fix the inferred type of a chain of three or more pipes (PHP 8.5), such as `$i |> abs(...) |> strval(...) |> strlen(...) |> strval(...)`, which could be the type of an earlier stage (`int` instead of `string` here). Phan caches the types of nodes by object id, and created a new temporary call node for a pipe each time it was looked at, which could get the id and the cached type of an earlier one
- Use the name of a parameter of a closure type that declares one (`Closure(int $count):void`) in the issues about arguments of calls to it, instead of `$p0`, `$p1`, ...

- Fix a crash of the fallback parser (`--use-fallback-parser`, `--force-polyfill-parser`, the language server) in PHP 8.6 for a binary, octal or hexadecimal integer literal that does not fit in an int, such as `0xffffffffffffffff`: `bindec()`, `hexdec()` and `octdec()` emit a notice for such a number in PHP 8.6. The fallback parser now converts these literals to the same float as php does, which it did not for binary literals (`bindec()` rounds differently) or for hexadecimal literals containing the digit `e`
